question: If $\begin{bmatrix}2x & 5 \\ 12 & x\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}6 & -5 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, then the value of $x$ is:
explanation:
Step 1 Expand the $2 \times 2$ determinant on the left side of the equation by multiplying the main diagonal elements and subtracting the product of the off-diagonal elements: $(2x)(x) - (5)(12) = 2x^2 - 60$.

Step 2 Expand the $2 \times 2$ determinant on the right side of the equation using the same cross-multiplication rule: $(6)(3) - (-5)(4) = 18 + 20 = 38$.

Step 3 Equate the two evaluated expressions to solve for the unknown variable $x$: $2x^2 - 60 = 38 \implies 2x^2 = 98 \implies x^2 = 49$. Taking the square root of both sides yields $x = \pm 7$, which matches option C.
